stem.text: Let y = f(x) be the solution to the differential equation \( \frac{dy}{dx} = 2 - 2 y \) with \( f(2) = 4 \). It is known that \( f(x) > 1 \) for all x. The line tangent to the graph of f at \( x = 2 \) is used to approximate \( f(\frac{5}{2}) \). Is the approximation an overestimate or an underestimate of the value of the solution? Give a reason for your answer.

answer_key.label: An underestimate, because the second derivative of f is positive for all x in the interval, so the graph of f is concave up there.

worked_solution.text: Differentiate the right side with respect to x and replace dy/dx by the equation: \( \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 4 \left(y - 1\right) \).
worked_solution.rule_named: implicit differentiation of the differential equation

worked_solution.text: Because \( f(x) > 1 \) for every x, the factor \( y - 1 \) is positive throughout, so the second derivative is positive on the whole interval from \( x = 2 \) to \( x = \frac{5}{2} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the second derivative over the interval

worked_solution.text: The graph of f is concave up there, so it lies above its tangent lines, and the approximation is an underestimate.
worked_solution.rule_named: direction of the error from concavity

options.label: An overestimate, because the first derivative of f is negative for all x in the interval, so f is decreasing there.
options.derivation: the direction decided from whether the solution increases or decreases, with no reference to concavity

options.label: An underestimate, because the second derivative of f is positive for all x in the interval, so the graph of f is concave up there.
An overestimate, because a tangent line approximation follows the slope at the point of tangency, and that slope is too steep for the rest of the interval.
options.derivation: a direction asserted from how the method works, with no concavity statement

options.label: An underestimate, because the second derivative of f is positive at the starting point, so the graph of f is concave up at that point.
options.derivation: the sign of the second derivative checked only at the starting point, a local fact offered where the interval is needed
